cluster_summary: A set of vulnerabilities caused by missing or insufficient validation of user-supplied data used in file path construction, file upload/download, and resource access. Common weaknesses include lack of path canonicalization, absence of file extension/MIME type allow-lists, missing inline disposition allow-lists, and failure to enforce size limits, leading to path traversal, arbitrary file upload, XSS, SSRF, and disk exhaustion.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs into the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs. Report code paths where the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect. Confirm that the guard is enforced before the sensitive effect and remains bound to the same resource, principal, destination, or object that the effect uses. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 4 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should Introduce a configurable allow-list of permitted file extensions and MIME types; reject files not on the list..

mechanism.source_shape: attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs
mechanism.typical_fix: Introduce a configurable allow-list of permitted file extensions and MIME types; reject files not on the list.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Introduce a configurable allow-list of permitted file extensions and MIME types; reject files not on the list.
sub_patterns.name: Missing file type validation (extension/MIME allow-list) in upload
sub_patterns.root_cause: File upload handlers accept any file without checking its extension or MIME type against a configured allow-list, allowing arbitrary file types (e.g., SVG, executable scripts) to be stored.
